The Nigeria Police Force has arrested eight suspected kidnappers and arms dealers and killed two armed men during separate operations targeting criminal networks across several states. The police said it also recovered 16 firearms, including a general-purpose machine gun and a grenade launcher. The Force Public Relations Officer, Ani Iniedu, disclosed in a statement on Tuesday, adding that the operations, conducted between October 10 and November 8, 2026, also led to the recovery of 1,000 rounds of live ammunition. Iniedu stated that five suspects were arrested during the first operation for their alleged involvement in a kidnapping and armed robbery syndicate operating across Kaduna, Jigawa, Katsina and Kano states. He identified them as Auwalu Yakubu Kura, 35; Hamisu Yasu, 35; Sabo Gambo, 34; Sulaiman Musa, 27; and Haruna Adamu, 19. The FPO noted that investigations indicated that the syndicate, allegedly led by Kura, had operated for more than six years and recruited younger members to sustain its network. He added that forensic and investigative findings had allegedly linked the suspects to several incidents involving kidnapping, armed robbery and culpable homicide. He stated, “Those in custody are Auwalu Yakubu Kura, male, 35, of Dogarawa, Zaria LGA, Kaduna State; Hamisu Yasu, male, 35, of Giwa LGA, Kaduna State; Sabo Gambo, male, 34, of Sabon Titi, Pan-Shekara, Kumbotso LGA, Kano State; as well as Sulaiman Musa, male, 27, and Haruna Adamu, male, 19. He identified the suspects as Aminu Ibrahim, 33; Masa’ud Bala, 35; and Idris Ahmed, 43. According to him, Ibrahim was arrested on November 7 in Gode Forest along the Mai’Adua-Koza axis of Katsina State, while Bala was apprehended during a follow-up operation in Daura. Iniedu stated that investigations indicated that Bala coordinated the movement of weapons from foreign suppliers, while Ibrahim allegedly served as a local courier, delivering firearms to armed bandit groups in Nigeria. He added that Ahmed was arrested on November 8 at Magama, Toro LGA of Bauchi State, over his alleged involvement in distributing arms across the North-East, North-West and North-Central regions. The FPRO noted that the arrest was followed by a gun battle after armed members of Ahmed’s gang opened fire on the approaching operatives. “In the ensuing gun battle, two armed assailants sustained gunshot injuries and were evacuated to a hospital for medical treatment, where they were confirmed dead by doctors and deposited at the morgue,” he added. Iniedu listed the recovered weapons as one General Purpose Machine Gun, four AK-47 rifles, seven AK-100 rifles, three M16 CQ rifles and one Milkor grenade launcher. Other exhibits recovered included 1,000 rounds of 7.62 x 54mm GPMG ammunition, seven empty rifle magazines, a Kia Sorento SUV, a Volkswagen Golf, a Galaxy van and a Daylong motorcycle. He added that the recovered firearms and ammunition were undergoing forensic and ballistic analysis, while efforts were ongoing to arrest other members of the syndicates. The FPRO noted that the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, commended the operatives for their professionalism and urged them to sustain efforts to dismantle criminal networks and disrupt the supply of illegal firearms. Iniedu urged members of the public to provide credible information to the police and warned against confronting armed suspects or taking the law into their own hands.
